method: Primary government sources and the live MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base were checked against vendor taxonomy claims. Shared names alone are not treated as proof of exact identity.

sources.title: Kimsuky, Group G0094
sources.analyst_notes: Lists APT43 as an associated group name while warning that DPRK cluster boundaries overlap.

sources.title: APT43: North Korean Group Uses Cybercrime to Fund Espionage Operations
sources.analyst_notes: Mandiant defines APT43 from its own collection and notes collaboration with other DPRK operators.

sources.title: APT41, Group G0096
sources.analyst_notes: Explicitly describes only partial overlap with Winnti Group and BARIUM reporting.

sources.title: Sandworm Team, Group G0034
sources.analyst_notes: Separates GRU Unit 74455 from APT28/Unit 26165 and documents assistance in some operations.

sources.title: Andariel, Group G0138
sources.analyst_notes: Describes Andariel as a subset of Lazarus Group and warns about overlapping DPRK taxonomies.

sources.title: Treasury Sanctions North Korean State-Sponsored Malicious Cyber Groups
sources.analyst_notes: Calls Bluenoroff and Andariel sub-groups of Lazarus and attributes all three to the RGB.

sources.title: Three North Korean Military Hackers Indicted in Wide-Ranging Scheme
sources.analyst_notes: Treats activity researchers label Lazarus Group and APT38 as participants in one alleged conspiracy; this does not erase private-sector cluster distinctions.

relationships.description: MITRE treats APT43 as an associated Kimsuky group name, while Mandiant defines APT43 using its own collection scope. The overlap is well supported, but exact one-to-one identity is not.
relationships.limitations: Vendor collection boundaries differ; do not replace both profiles with a single exact alias record.
relationships.counterevidence: The sources support overlap but do not establish that every APT43 observation belongs to the narrower Kimsuky activity set.

relationships.description: MITRE states that APT41 overlaps at least partially with public reporting on Winnti Group.
relationships.limitations: Partial overlap is not exact identity and does not imply all Winnti-umbrella activity is APT41.
relationships.counterevidence: An exact-alias assertion would be stronger than the cited source supports.

relationships.description: Some Sandworm/GRU Unit 74455 operations were conducted with assistance from APT28/GRU Unit 26165.
relationships.limitations: The actors are attributed to distinct GRU units and must remain separate profiles.
relationships.counterevidence: Shared operations do not support treating Sandworm and APT28 as aliases.

relationships.description: MITRE considers Andariel a subset of Lazarus Group; U.S. Treasury also describes Andariel as a Lazarus subgroup controlled by the RGB.
relationships.limitations: Lazarus is also used as a broad umbrella label in some reporting, so operation-level attribution should retain the Andariel label where supported.
relationships.counterevidence: The sources warn that DPRK cluster boundaries overlap; subgroup status does not imply identical tooling across all Lazarus activity.

relationships.description: Government sources connect Bluenoroff/APT38 and Lazarus under the RGB and a common conspiracy, while industry reporting preserves APT38 as a financially focused cluster.
relationships.limitations: APT38, Bluenoroff, and Lazarus have vendor-dependent scopes; exact equivalence should not be asserted.
relationships.counterevidence: The DOJ's common-conspiracy framing is organizational/legal and does not prove identical operational clustering.
